thread:
alerts-bot: [ALERT] spike in 5xxs on /v1/generate (hosted-us-east). ~6% 5xx over last 5m, p95 latency 18s. Affected pool: model-pool-prod. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/latency/hosted-us-east?orgId=1

Lee (support): Customer ACME reported multiple 504/502s starting ~09:12 UTC. They say requests hang ~15-20s then gateway 504. Also a couple customers saw auth failures (401) in the same window. Escalating to oncall.

Maya (oncall): I'm digging in. Quick checks: kube events for model-pool-prod namespace show a bunch of HPA/POD events. Copying clipped output:```
$ kubectl -n hosted-us-east get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Deployment --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 30
2026-03-15T09:11:44Z  Warning  FailedCreate  replicaset/model-serving-5xx  Error creating: pods "model-serving-" is forbidden: exceeded quota
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z  Normal   ScalingReplicaSet  HorizontalPodAutoscaler  Scaled up replica set model-serving-5xx (status: 0->1)
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z  Warning  FailedScheduling  default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient memory, 3 node(s) didn't match node selector, 3 node(s) had taints.
2026-03-15T09:12:30Z  Normal   SuccessfulCreate  replicaset/model-serving-5xx  Created pod: model-serving-5xx-abcde
2026-03-15T09:12:46Z  Warning  ReadinessProbeFailed  pod/model-serving-5xx-abcde  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
2026-03-15T09:13:10Z  Warning  BackoffLimitExceeded  scaledobject/keda-adapter  Reconciliation gave up: scaling backoff
```

Maya: That readyness probe failure line is the smoking gun — pods are created but not Ready due to the model init path returning 503 until the model is fully loaded. KEDA shows backoff, so it stops trying to scale further.

Priya (infra): Adding context: our model-serving image lazy-loads model weights on first request, and the cold-start load plus decompression takes ~9-12s on these instances (we measured earlier). Readiness probe is hitting `/health` which returns 503 until weights loaded. KEDA ScaledObject has pollingInterval: 30s and cooldownPeriod: 300s; HPA stabilization window is 300s. With a big burst, KEDA scales to 1->2 but then backoff and HPA doesn't force more replicas because metrics window smooths it out.

Priya (infra): Current scaledobject snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-serving-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: deployment/model-serving
  pollingInterval: 30 # secs
  cooldownPeriod: 300 # secs
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring.svc
      metricName: custom_queue_length
      threshold: '50'
```

Tomas (runtime): On top of cold start, runtime falls back to a slower quantized path for some model variants which adds ~6s. Also KV-cache warmup (first few tokens) increases latency. If probe requires full model readiness (weights + cache) we wait longer than necessary. Suggest readiness return 200 after weights bound but allow traffic drain to warm cache asynchronously.

Eric (sre): I also see auth token churn in the logs at the same time: our auth-proxy logged bursts of 401s from `/auth/validate` between 09:11:50-09:13:20 UTC. Snippet:```json
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] WARN auth-proxy - token validation failed for clientToken=tok_abc123 : 401 Unauthorized (token lookup timeout)
[2026-03-15T09:12:08Z] WARN auth-proxy - token cache miss, fetching from billing-service
[2026-03-15T09:12:12Z] ERROR billing-client - rate limited when reading account state: 429 Too Many Requests
[2026-03-15T09:12:14Z] WARN auth-proxy - fallback to synchronous billing read -> latency 1.2s
```

Eric: So two failure modes combine: (1) autoscaling stalls because readiness probe blocks and KEDA/HPA backoff prevents quick ramp; (2) auth/billing reads get rate-limited leading to 401s or added latency so gateway returns 502/504 for clients who time out waiting.

Lee (support): Customer reported they retried a few times and got success after ~30s. They want repro steps and ETA to mitigate.

Tomas (runtime): Quick mitigation steps we can run now (non-invasive):
1) patch readiness probe to be less strict so pod becomes Ready earlier (return 200 once weights are mapped but before full cache warm).
2) reduce KEDA pollingInterval to 5s and cooldownPeriod to 60s temporarily for model-pool-prod scaledobject.
3) set HPA.minReplicas to 2 for model-serving deployment while we monitor.

Commands to apply (run in order):```bash
# patch readiness to soft check
kubectl -n hosted-us-east patch deployment model-serving --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/health/soft"}]'
# reduce keda polling and cooldown
kubectl -n hosted-us-east patch scaledobject model-serving-scaledobject --type='merge' -p='{"spec":{"pollingInterval":5,"cooldownPeriod":60}}'
# bump min replicas
kubectl -n hosted-us-east patch hpa model-serving --type='merge' -p='{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
```

Priya (infra): I'll run the KEDA/HPA patches now and watch events. We should also ensure quota/limits don't prevent new pods — I saw a quota error earlier; I'll increase deployment resource quota for the namespace temporarily.

deploy-bot: Canary patch starting: deployment/model-serving -> image model-serving:2026-03-15-hotfix-1 (rollout 1/3)

Kate (cust-succ): I'll message ACME with a short RCA: "We saw a transient scale-up delay combined with auth service rate limiting; we applied a temporary config to reduce autoscaler cooldown and make readiness less strict. We expect traffic to recover and will follow up with permanent fixes and an RCA within 24h."

Maya (oncall): Repro steps we used for internal test:```bash
# simulate burst of 250 concurrent small requests to /v1/generate
hey -n 2500 -c 250 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_XXXXX" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}' https://hosted-us-east.internal/v1/generate
# observe: pods created but many fail readiness -> p95 latency spikes and gateway 504s
```

Maya (oncall): After applying patches p95 latency dropped from 18s -> 1.8s within 60s and 5xx rate back to baseline. Monitoring graphs: scaled replicas climbed to 3, readiness successes increased.

Eric (sre): Longer-term actions assigned:
- Add pre-warmed standby pool of 1-2 pods per model-pool (owner: infra / Priya).
- Make readiness probe tiered: weights-mapped -> Ready; cache-warm async (owner: runtime / Tomas).
- Adjust KEDA default polling to 5s for bursty queues and lower cooldown for model pools (owner: infra).
- Harden auth-proxy to use batched billing reads + exponential backoff to avoid 429 cascading (owner: platform-auth).
- Add synthetic warmup probe: send a single token sampling request to new replicas to warm KV cache before marking Ready (owner: runtime).

Lee (support): ACME updated: they confirmed recovery at ~09:15 UTC and accepted the temporary mitigation. Asking for an RCA doc + timeline for permanent fix.

Kate (cust-succ): I'll schedule a follow-up meeting with ACME tomorrow; keep me posted if we change any configs.

Priya (infra): Quota bump and keda/hpa patches applied at 09:13:05 UTC. Watching for regressions.

Maya (oncall): Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will keep thread open until permanent fixes are in flight.

Tomas (runtime): I'll open PR for readiness probe change + warmup probe and link to this thread.

Eric (sre): Opening a postmortem template and will assign action items.

---
Summary: Cause = slow model cold-start + strict readiness + KEDA/HPA cooldown/backoff + auth/billing throttling. Impact = transient 5xx/504 for hosted inference during bursts. Mitigation = relax readiness, reduce KEDA polling & cooldown, bump minReplicas, temporary quota increase. Owners assigned for durable fixes.
